title: Sunscreen SPF50

drivers.name: Price increase (4.1%)
drivers.evidence: At $13.93 (same as target), sales averaged 24.0 (vs baseline 24.9), a 3.6% drop. With 4.1% price hike and no promotion, and consistent pattern in recent weeks, a -8% effect is justified. Noise-adjusted and calibrated to past price sensitivity.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 24.9. The target week has no event or promotion, but the price is raised 4.1% above regular ($13.38 → $13.93). Recent weeks show a consistent price sensitivity: at $13.93 (same as 2026-09-28–10-05), sales dropped to 27–21 units (vs baseline 24.9), suggesting a price effect. The 4.1% increase is likely to reduce demand. Historical data shows no promotion in this price range, and uplift model suggests no effect. Noise-adjusted evidence from past price hikes (no promotions) supports a modest downside. No seasonal or event driver is present.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 13.93 (+4.1% vs regular price 13.38)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 24.9 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 62.7 | 10%-90%: 2.9 - 43.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
